claim: For every integer \(N\ge4\), there are two coarsening filtrations of finite topologies on the same \(N\)-point set whose uniform normalized minimal-open discrepancy is \(1/N^2\), while the degree-one bottleneck distance of the induced persistence diagrams is exactly \(1\). Consequently, no constant \(C\) independent of \(N\) can bound \(d_B\le C\Delta_N\) for all such filtrations.

scientific_limitations_and_integrity.integrity: Self-review only; independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.
not_claimed: No claim about the density-based metric-generated subclass.
No claim about practical profile/adaptive or anchor-selected constructions.
No claim that bounds depending on N or additional structural hypotheses are impossible.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.proved: Exact degree-one barcode separation and failure of any dimension-independent Lipschitz bound from the normalized minimal-open discrepancy alone.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.reproducibility: A standard-library verification script enumerates the finite order complexes and exact rational boundary ranks; the integral homology follows from explicit cycle and disk descriptions.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity.scope: Abstract coarsening filtrations of finite topologies on a shared N-point set.

title: A normalized finite-topology discrepancy has no dimension-free bottleneck bound
